prompt: What does a prompt cache store?
hint: The answer is still written fresh every time.

choices.text: The answers to earlier calls, so that a repeated question is answered from memory
choices.why: Nothing about the answer is stored; it is generated on every call.

choices.text: The work of reading the start of a prompt
choices.why: Right: a later call starting with the same tokens skips that part.

choices.text: The whole conversation with a customer
choices.why: It keeps no conversation; it matches prefixes of prompts.

choices.text: The customer's message, to save tokens
choices.why: The message is the part that varies, and the least reusable.

prompt: In the stand-in, a prompt's first block differs from every earlier call's, but blocks 2 to 7 match one exactly. How many tokens are read from the cache?
hint: The run of matching blocks starts at the first.

choices.text: 192, the six blocks that match
choices.why: A block is only read when every block before it matched.

choices.text: 224, since the whole prompt is cached
choices.why: Block 1 differs, so nothing after it is reused.

choices.text: None
choices.why: Right: the first block ends the run before it starts.

choices.text: 32, the first block only
choices.why: The first block is the one that differs.

prompt: Below how many tokens does the stand-in never cache a prompt?
Which statement about real providers' caches does the lesson make?
hint: Some cache by themselves; some where you mark it.

choices.text: They all use 32-token blocks and a 64-token minimum, exactly like the stand-in does
choices.why: Those are the course's numbers, not any provider's.

choices.text: They cache whole conversations, so a customer's earlier messages are never sent twice
choices.why: They cache a prefix of a prompt.

choices.text: They match a prefix, with their own sizes, minimums, time limits and prices
choices.why: Right: read your provider's documentation for the model you call.

choices.text: They never charge for writing
choices.why: The lesson says nothing so absolute; prices are theirs to set.

prompt: Why did turning the cache on for `v1-bare` change nothing in `pl cost`?
hint: Look at the input per call.

choices.text: At 36.5 tokens a call, no prompt reached the 64-token minimum for caching
choices.why: Right: a prompt under the minimum is never cached.

choices.text: `--set` cannot turn the cache on
choices.why: It can; `cache` is one of the parameters.

choices.text: The bare prompt has no JSON
choices.why: Format has nothing to do with caching.

choices.text: The cache only works on holdout
choices.why: It works on any test set.

prompt: `v17-message-first` read 0 tokens from the cache over forty calls. Why?
hint: What is in its first block?

choices.text: The cache was off
choices.why: It wrote 9312 tokens, so it was on.

choices.text: Its first block holds the message
choices.why: Right, and a block is only read when every block before it matched.

choices.text: The prompt was under the 64-token minimum for caching
choices.why: It is about 250 tokens a call, far above 64.

choices.text: The guide was too long to fit into the cache's blocks
choices.why: Length is no obstacle; position is.

prompt: `v17-static-first` read 8736 tokens from the cache; every call but the first read the same number. How many tokens did each of those calls read?
hint: Forty calls, and the first had nothing to read.

prompt: What is the rule for ordering a cached prompt?
hint: The cache matches from the start.

choices.text: The fixed part first, what varies last
choices.why: Right: the shared prefix is what can be reused.

choices.text: The message first, so that the model reads it while it is fresh
choices.why: That is the order that read nothing from the cache.

choices.text: Alphabetical order of the sections
choices.why: Order matters for what is shared, not for the alphabet.

choices.text: It makes no difference to a cache
choices.why: It made the difference between 3.0302 and 6.0216 cents.

prompt: A block is read from the cache only when every block ___ it matched as well.
hint: Its position relative to the blocks that come first.

prompt: With the cache on, `v17-static-first` paid for 10139 input tokens, as `v8-guide` did without it. What did the cache change?

choices.text: The number of tokens the model read
choices.why: Both read 10139.

choices.text: The output tokens, which the cache shortened
choices.why: Output was 1536 in both; a cache only touches the prompt.

choices.text: What each token cost
choices.why: Right: most were read at a tenth of the price.

choices.text: The answers, which became shorter and therefore cheaper to produce
choices.why: The answers were identical, message by message.

prompt: At the lab's prices, how much does one block of 32 tokens cost to write to the cache, in millionths of a cent?
With the lab's prices, from which use does a cached block start costing less than reading it plain every time?
hint: Written once at 375, then read at 30; plain is 300 each time.

choices.text: From the first
choices.why: Once: 375 against 300. A prefix used once costs more cached.

choices.text: From the second
choices.why: Right: 375 + 30 = 405 against 600.

choices.text: From the tenth, because a read costs a tenth of plain input
choices.why: The tenth is the read price, not the break-even.

choices.text: Never, because a write always costs more than it saves
choices.why: The guide-first run saved 43%.

prompt: `v17-message-first` cost more with the cache than the same calls without it. Why?
hint: What happened to the 9312 cached tokens?

choices.text: Its answers were longer
choices.why: Output was 1521 tokens against 1536; shorter, not longer.

choices.text: The cache charges a fee per call on top of the token prices
choices.why: There is no per-call fee in `prices.json`.

choices.text: Reading from the cache costs more than plain input
choices.why: A read costs a tenth of plain input, and it read nothing anyway.

choices.text: Its writes went unread
choices.why: Right: 9312 × 75 millionths of a cent for nothing.

prompt: A team adds the date at the top of a cached prompt: *Today is 14 August.* What happens to the cache?

choices.text: Nothing, because the date is short
choices.why: Length does not matter; position does.

choices.text: Every block after the date is new each day, so the guide is written again daily
choices.why: Right. Put the date at the end, with the message.

choices.text: Only the block holding the date is rewritten each day; the guide after it is still read
choices.why: A block only matches if everything before it matches.

choices.text: The cache refuses prompts with dates
choices.why: It refuses nothing; it just stops matching.

prompt: `pl compare` of `v8-guide` against `v17-static-first` printed `fixed 0, broken 0`. What does that establish?
hint: Same template, cache off and on.

choices.text: The cache made the prompt better
choices.why: Nothing was fixed.

choices.text: Turning the cache on changed no result on any message
choices.why: Right: cost and time changed, the answers did not.

choices.text: The two prompts use different models
choices.why: Same model, same template.

choices.text: The cache is broken and did not run on any of the forty calls at all
choices.why: It read 8736 tokens; it ran.

prompt: A new example is inserted near the top of a cached guide. Why do blocks whose text did not change stop being read?
hint: Blocks are cut by position, from the start.

choices.text: It shifts every token after it, so each later block now holds different tokens
choices.why: Right, and each block's key covers every block before it as well.

choices.text: The cache is cleared by every commit
choices.why: The cache knows nothing about commits.

choices.text: Examples are never cached
choices.why: Fixed examples are exactly what a cache is for.

choices.text: The prompt became too long
choices.why: Length is not the problem; the shift is.

prompt: Moving the message first changed which replies passed (5 fixed, 3 broken). What does the capture say caused it?
hint: All forty categories agree, and every difference is in `json`.

choices.text: The cache returned stale answers
choices.why: A cache stores no answers, and cache on and off agreed on every message.

choices.text: The reorder changed the text, and the stand-in's formatting habits fell on other messages
choices.why: Right: same rate, different messages. A reorder is a prompt change.

choices.text: The model misread the guide when it came second
choices.why: Every category and urgency matched; only the wrapping moved.

choices.text: The sign test proved the message-first order better
choices.why: At 0.727 it proved nothing either way.

prompt: Order the parts of a cached triage prompt from first to last.
items: The instructions and the guide to the categories

prompt: Match each run to what the cache did in it.

pairs.right: Nothing at all: under the minimum
Cache off: all 10139 tokens plain input

prompt: A colleague turns the cache on and moves the examples to the end of the prompt in the same commit. The bill falls and the score drops by two. What should happen next?
hint: Two changes, one of them to the text.

choices.text: Keep it: caching never changes answers, so the two points are noise from the stand-in's habits
choices.why: Moving the examples changed the text, and that can change answers.

choices.text: Turn the cache off again
choices.why: The cache is the part least likely to have moved the score.

choices.text: Split it: the cache alone, then the reorder through the gate with its broken messages named
choices.why: Right: a cache should change only cost; a reorder is a prompt change.

choices.text: Move the message to the top as well
choices.why: That would cost the cache everything after it.
